objective.value: Test whether E. coli can optimally utilize multiple alternative carbon sources via serial adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) first in L-lactate then glycerol and vice versa; elucidate the genetic and transcriptomic basis of serial adaptation; and assess serial-ALE strains for acetoin bioproduction under single and mixed-carbon conditions.
objective.notes: Abstract and Introduction final paragraph state the objective directly.

hypothesis.value: Serial (sequential single-carbon) ALE across two fitness landscapes yields a single dominant generalist lineage with universal growth advantage on both carbon sources and their mixture, avoiding the fitness trade-offs or specialist subpopulations seen in mixed-carbon ALE, and the resulting rewired physiology improves bioproduction of a value-added product (acetoin).

inference.rationale: No explicit formal hypothesis statement; inferred from 'To test whether a bacterial strain can optimally utilize multiple carbon sources' (abstract) and Discussion statement that serial ALE is expected to enable evolution of a single dominant generalist instead of co-existing sub-populations.

hypothesis.notes: Authors frame expectations but do not label a formal hypothesis.

strain.value: Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 wild-type (parental/ancestor); phase-1 evolved strains LA (lactate-adapted) and GL (glycerol-adapted); serial-ALE end-point strains LA-GL and GL-LA; LA and LA-GL derivatives with mutT and dam restored at the lacZ locus (used as acetoin production hosts); reconstructed single/sequential mutants in MG1655 background.
strain.notes: Strain list and plasmids deferred to Supplementary Table S1 (not available); lineage nomenclature LA/GL/LA-GL/GL-LA defined in Results 2.1. 'wild type' paper label corresponds to standard lab strain MG1655, not a natural isolate.

genotype.value: Adaptive mutations tracked by WGS: LA lineage - rph-pyrE 69 bp deletion (rph 619del69, E207fs; first fixed by generation 50), hfq (142 A>T), cyaA (reported as 2336 T>G in 2.2 and 2236 T>G in 2.4 - unresolved), ppsA (72 T>G), ydcI (5 A>C); GL lineage - rpoC (3610del9, V1204fs), glpK (694 G>T, G232C); second phase added ppsA (13 G>T, G5R), ydcI (686-7insG, G229fs), hdfR (463 G>T, E155*), glpK (189 A>C); mutator phenotypes of LA and LA-GL attributed to mutT and dam mutations, restored with wild-type mutT and dam at lacZ. rpoC mutant excluded from reverse engineering (essential gene difficulty).
genotype.notes: Fig. 1D table in extracted markdown has empty frequency cells; exact allele-frequency trajectories require figure rendering/supplement. cyaA nucleotide-change notation inconsistent between sections (see conflicts).

engineering_method.value: Two-phase serial adaptive laboratory evolution (serial passage at mid-exponential phase, ~800 generations per carbon source, 1400-1600 generations total); lambda-Red one-step inactivation/recombineering (Datsenko-Wanner) with pKD13 kanamycin cassette, overlap-extension PCR and pCP20 marker excision for reverse engineering of single, sequential and double mutants; restoration of mutT/dam at lacZ locus; episomal heterologous expression of Bacillus subtilis alsS and Aeromonas hydrophila alsD from plasmid pTrcHis2A-alsSD (IPTG-inducible).
engineering_method.notes: pTrcHis2A-alsSD was constructed in a previous study (Choe et al., 2022) - background element, not a design decision of this paper.

experimental_groups.value: ALE: three independent populations per lineage direction (LA->LA-GL and GL->GL-LA). Phenotyping: WT, LA, GL, LA-GL, GL-LA each in M9 glycerol, M9 lactate, and M9 mix; also acetate, D-xylose, D-glucose, LB, TB. Reverse engineering: 11 single/sequential mutants from LA-GL mutation set and 7 from GL-LA set in WT background, assayed in glycerol, lactate, and mixed conditions; double mutants glpK(694G>T)-rph-pyrE(del) and ppsA(13G>T)-rph-pyrE(del). Transcriptomics: WT and end-point strains in respective evolutionary media and mixed-carbon (10 datasets, 1205 DEGs). Biolog PM1/PM2A respiration profiling. Acetoin production: WT, GL, GL-LA carrying pTrcHis2A-alsSD in M9 glycerol, M9 lactate, M9 mix with casamino acids.
experimental_groups.notes: Methods 4.2 says 'Two independent lineages' (the two lineage directions), Results 2.1 says 'Three independent populations' were serially passaged - recorded as minor ambiguity, interpreted as 3 populations per direction.

controls.value: E. coli MG1655 wild-type as ancestral/unevolved comparator in all growth, uptake, transcriptome, cAMP, Biolog and acetoin assays; single-ALE ancestors LA and GL as comparators for serial-ALE end-point strains; negative-control wells (AUC baseline) in Biolog phenotype microarray to discriminate false-negative growth; 'control__wt_glc' sample used as baseline control for iModulon ICA against the PRECISE compendium.
controls.notes: No empty-plasmid/no-pathway negative control for acetoin production is reported in the main text.

culture_conditions.value: 30 C, oxic. ALE: 60 mL M9 minimal in 300 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, 200 rpm shaking, serial transfer twice daily at OD600 0.4-0.6 (mid-exponential), initial OD adjusted downward as growth improved. Plate-reader growth assays: 48-well, 300 uL working volume, 807 rpm double orbital, 30 C, 24 h, OD600 every 30 min. Biolog: 30 C, 48 h on OmniLog. Acetoin batch production: 60 mL, 30 C with shaking, 24 h, supernatant sampled every 2 h. Pre-cultures: 3 mL M9 with matched carbon source.
culture_conditions.notes: Cell-stock temperature printed as '80 C glycerol cell stocks' - minus sign lost in parsing; physically implies -80 C (see conflicts).

medium.value: M9 minimal medium (M9 salts, 2 mM MgSO4, 0.1 mM CaCl2) with either 0.2% (v/v) L-lactate or 0.2% (v/v) glycerol as sole carbon source; M9 mix (0.1% v/v each of glycerol and L-lactate); acetoin production media: M9 glycerol / M9 lactate / M9 mix each supplemented with 0.2% Casamino Acids and 100 ug/mL ampicillin; LB agar with 50 ug/mL kanamycin for recombineering selection; LB for pCP20 curing at 42 C; enriched LB and Terrific Broth for non-adaptive growth profiling; Biolog IF-0a GN/GP inoculating fluid with PM1/PM2A plates.
medium.notes: Only L-lactate (not D/DL mixtures) used unless stated otherwise.

dosage.value: Carbon sources: 0.2% v/v L-lactate or glycerol (single), 0.1% v/v each (mix); non-adaptive carbons: sodium acetate 0.2% v/v, D-xylose 0.2% w/v, D-glucose 0.2% w/v; kanamycin 50 ug/mL; ampicillin 100 ug/mL; IPTG 10 uM added 2 h post-inoculation; Casamino Acids 0.2%; Biolog inoculum OD600 = 0.05; cAMP assay cell input ~20 mL of OD600 = 1.0 culture.
dosage.notes: Methods 4.13 prints 'M9 lactate (0.2 v/v L-lactate)' with missing % sign (typo).

time.value: ALE: ~800 generations phase 1, then 600-800 generations phase 2 (1400-1600 total); WGS sampling every 50 generations; growth assays 24 h with OD600 at 30-min intervals; Biolog respiration 48 h; acetoin batch 24 h with supernatant sampling at 2 h intervals; IPTG induction at 2 h post-inoculation; RNASnap lysis 95 C 7 min; cAMP lysis 20 min at room temperature.
time.notes: ALE duration expressed in generations, not calendar time; per-passage wall time not reported.

replicates.value: Three independent ALE populations per lineage direction (independent_culture_replicates, biological_independence=likely); growth/fitness assays and SGR/CUR comparisons: biological triplicates (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 captions, SD error bars); acetoin production: three biological replicates (Fig. 4 caption); Biolog PM: biological triplicates; cAMP ELISA: each sample assayed in duplicates (technical replicates); RNA-seq replicate counts not stated in main text (requires supplement).
replicates.notes: RNA-seq replicate structure and per-mutant growth-assay replicate counts not visible in main text - requires_supplement.

assay.value: Doubling time per passage from initial/final OD of serial transfers (fitness trajectory); specific growth rate (SGR) from OD600 time series; specific carbon uptake rate (CUR) by HPLC of spent media; whole-genome resequencing for mutation trajectories; reconstructed-mutant fitness assay (percent contribution = mutant SGR relative to end-point strain SGR); RNA-seq transcriptomics with PCA, DEG and iModulon/ICA analysis; intracellular cAMP ELISA (colorimetric, non-acetylation protocol); Biolog PM1/PM2A specific respiration rates (AUC); maximum acetoin specific productivity from HPLC time courses.

instruments.value: BioTek Epoch2 / Synergy HT plate readers; Shimadzu Nexera LC-40 HPLC with RID-20A RI detector and Agilent MetaCarb 87H column (0.007 N H2SO4, 0.6 mL/min, 50 C or 65 C for mixed-carbon); Covaris S220 ultrasonicator; Qubit 2.0 fluorometer; Illumina HiSeq 2500 (50-cycle SE, WGS) and HiSeq X Ten (150-cycle PE, RNA-seq); TapeStation 2200 with High Sensitivity D1000; Bio-Rad MicroPulser electroporator; Biolog OmniLog.

analysis_methods.value: CLC Genomics Workbench read trimming/mapping to NC_000913.3 (mismatch cost 2, indel cost 3, length/similarity 0.9); Quality-based Variant Detection (min coverage 10, min variant frequency 10%); mutation causality triangulation via recurrence across ALE studies and ALEdb; DESeq2 normalization and fold-change; hierarchical clustering (Euclidean, complete); PCA; OptICA/iModulon analysis against PRECISE 278-dataset compendium (100 iterations, 1e-7 tolerance, DBSCAN robust components); student's independent t-test for Biolog AUC; pairwise significance testing with P<0.05/0.01/0.001 thresholds (full matrix in Table S3).
analysis_methods.notes: Abstract calls iModulon/ICA 'machine learning analysis'. Statistical test used for SGR/CUR/productivity comparisons not specified in main text (Table S3 in supplement).

outcomes.value: Serial-ALE end-point strains (LA-GL, GL-LA) showed generalist phenotype with significantly improved SGR/CUR in both glycerol and lactate and in the mixture without trade-offs on the first carbon (e.g., GL-LA +1.89x SGR, +1.73x CUR vs GL); mixed-carbon growth advantages 1.38-2.15x over WT. Four variants (glpK, ppsA, ydcI, rph-pyrE) accounted for >80% of end-point strain fitness; glpK/ppsA specialist effects vanished in mixed carbon and were rescued/strengthened by rph-pyrE(del) (double mutants: ~2x rph-pyrE single-mutant contribution for glpK pair, >=+8% for ppsA pair). Transcriptomes diverged lineage-specifically despite fitness convergence; RpoS/GadW iModulons decreased in all evolved strains; GlpR/LldR/Zur/Crp-2 activities condition-specific. glpK-mutant strains had up to 38% lower intracellular cAMP. 82 carbons with increased respiration in >=1 evolved strain, 36 concordant across all; evolved strains grew faster on acetate/xylose/glucose but showed fitness deficits in LB/TB. Acetoin: GL-LA specific productivity highest in all conditions; ~3.7x (GL-LA) and 2.9x (GL) vs WT in glycerol; GL-LA 1.3x over GL (glycerol), 1.6x/1.4x over WT/GL in lactate; superior in mixed condition.
outcomes.notes: Exact SGR/CUR/productivity values, error bars and full statistics reside in Table S3 / Supplementary Figs (requires_supplement); mechanism of rph-pyrE epistasis stated by authors as elusive - interpretation, not validated causality.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Evolve E. coli MG1655 sequentially on two alternative carbon sources to obtain generalist end-point strains and test serial-ALE as a strain-optimization scheme.
experimental_design_object.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (clonal ancestral population)
experimental_design_object.intervention: Two-phase serial ALE: phase 1 ~800 generations on M9+lactate (LA) or M9+glycerol (GL); carbon switch at fitness plateau; phase 2 600-800 generations on the other carbon (LA-GL, GL-LA); 60 mL M9 in 300 mL flasks, 30 C, 200 rpm, transfer twice daily at OD600 0.4-0.6.

conditions.medium: M9 minimal + 0.2% v/v single carbon per phase
conditions.selection: fastest-growing progeny via mid-exponential serial transfer

experimental_design_object.control: Wild-type MG1655 (fitness baseline); phase-1 ancestors LA/GL as comparators for end-point strains
experimental_design_object.readout: Doubling time per passage vs cumulative generation; end-point SGR and CUR in each carbon source
experimental_design_object.analysis: Fitness trajectory plateau detection; pairwise significance vs WT (Table S3)
experimental_design_object.outcome: End-point strains LA-GL and GL-LA acquired universal growth advantage on both single and mixed carbon sources without trade-off on the first carbon; GL showed trade-off in lactate (single-ALE specialist).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate initiation of an ALE/selection campaign; Q2: performed in this study; Q3: produced the chassis later chosen (GL-LA) for bioproduction, changing subsequent design choices.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integrated evolution/screening campaign generating strain variants rather than targeting a pre-specified genetic change.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: E. coli K-12 exhibits suboptimal fitness on glycerol and lactate, and prior single-carbon ALE studies showed such phenotypes can be reconfigured by evolution; whether sequential adaptation across two landscapes works was seldom explored.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Outcome measured directly (growth rates, uptake rates, WGS of evolving populations).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Choice of ALE and the 800-generation timescale explicitly built on prior studies (Ibarra 2002, Kang 2019, Sandberg 2019) rather than a newly derived mechanistic argument; sequential single-carbon design contrasted against prior mixed-carbon ALE (Sandberg 2017).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When optimizing E. coli for utilization of multiple metabolically related alternative carbon sources (e.g., gluconeogenic glycerol and L-lactate), apply serial single-carbon ALE phases (~800 generations each to fitness plateau) instead of simultaneous mixed-carbon evolution, because sequential adaptation fixed carbon-specialist plus generalist mutations and avoided fitness trade-offs and specialist subpopulation splitting in the tested two-carbon system.
alternatives_considered: Simultaneous mixed-carbon ALE (contrasted with Sandberg et al., 2017; avoided to evade trade-offs/bet-hedging)

ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When deploying ALE-derived E. coli lineages as production hosts, check and restore DNA-repair defects (e.g., mutT/dam mutator alleles) before pathway introduction, because mutator backgrounds accumulated during evolution destabilize the production genotype - validated here only for lactate/glycerol-evolved MG1655 lineages used for acetoin production.

unsupported_values: Develop a CRISPRi-based multi-gene combinatorial repression system in Escherichia coli that uses three orthogonal low-leakage inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD) to express three sgRNAs from a single plasmid (p3gRNA-LTA), so that all repression combinations of three target genes can be assessed by adding different inducer combinations instead of constructing numerous sgRNA plasmids; demonstrate utility by optimizing NeuAc biosynthesis via repression of PEP-consuming genes (pta, ptsI, pykA).

Orthogonal low-leakage inducible promoters driving independent sgRNAs, combined with sgRNA handle mutations that reduce dCas9 affinity, will eliminate leaky repression and enable rigorous combinatorial multi-gene repression by inducer addition; reducing PEP consumption (via pta/ptsI/pykA repression) will increase NeuAc accumulation because the DN5/pB3 strain accumulates ManNAc while PEP does not, suggesting PEP is limiting.

DN5: ΔnanATEK, ΔnagEBAC, ΔldhA, ΔpoxB, ΔackA in E. coli DH5α background (constructed previously, ref 29). MG1655RFP: ΔlacI, ΔgusR, native lacZ and gusA promoters replaced by constitutive promoters, rfp integrated into genome for constitutive expression. Plasmids: p3gRNA-LTA (three-sgRNA expression plasmid with BbsI, BsaI, SapI type IIS sites between PlacO1/PLtetO-1/ParaBAD promoters and sgRNA handle sequences; optimized version uses handle mutant #3 under PlacO1 and mutant #5 under PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD); pdCas9-3TFs (dCas9 plus transcription factors lacIAM, tetR, araC); pB3 (neuB, slr1975, GNA1, feedback-resistant glmS).

CRISPR interference (CRISPRi, dCas9) with three orthogonal inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD) each expressing one sgRNA; sgRNA handle sequence mutants (#3 for PlacO1, #5 for PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD) to reduce leaky repression by lowering dCas9 affinity; a modified one-step sequential Golden Gate Assembly method (Type IIS enzymes BbsI, BsaI, SapI; T4 DNA ligase + T4 PNK; 37°C 5 min / 25°C 15 min, ten cycles per round, with sequential addition of fragments in the same reaction mixture) for rapid three-sgRNA insertion into p3gRNA-LTA; Gibson assembly for general plasmid construction; genome engineering of MG1655 (lacI/gusR knockout, promoter replacement, rfp integration) for the reporter strain.
Promoter screen: 8 candidate inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD, PrhaBAD, PCymRC, PLuxB, PsalTTC, PCin) expressing mKate, each with and without its corresponding inducer (Fig. 2A).
Orthogonality test: 4 low-leakage promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD, PrhaBAD) × 4 inducers cross-design with mKate reporter (Fig. 2B).
Glucose interference: PrhaBAD induction by Rha with 10 g/L glucose present (Figure S2).
Leakiness/repression: sgRNA targeting rfp expressed from each of the three promoters, ± inducer (Fig. 4A-C).
sgRNA handle mutant screen: 7 handle mutants (#1-#7) expressing lacZ1-targeting sgRNA from each of the three promoters, ± inducer (Fig. 4D).
Target-site position: 3 sgRNAs each targeting lacZ and gusA from ParaBAD, ± inducer (Figures S4, S5).
Spacer length: 17, 22, 24, 27 bp spacers targeting lacZ1 site (Figure S6).
System characterization: MG1655RFP with p3gRNA-LTA (gusA-, rfp-, lacZ-targeting sgRNAs) under all inducer-combination conditions (Fig. 5).

NeuAc application: DN5/pB3 with p3gRNA-LTA carrying sgRNAs targeting pta, ptsI, pykA, under all 8 inducer on/off combinations (single: pta, ptsI, pykA; double: pta/ptsI, pta/pykA, ptsI/pykA; triple: pta/ptsI/pykA; plus no-inducer control) in 48 h shake-flask fermentation (Fig. 6B, Fig. 7).
rfp repression assays: strain constitutively expressing fluorescent protein without CRISPRi (Fig. 4A caption).
Promoter screen: same promoter constructs without inducer (baseline leakage measurement, Fig. 2A red circles).
System characterization (Fig. 5): strains without sgRNA targeting any genes; control enzyme activity/fluorescence normalized to 1.
NeuAc fermentation (Fig. 6B): strains without sgRNA targeting any genes as control; titers also expressed relative to 'wildtype' (= no-repression control, 100%).
Fermentation by-product detection (Fig. 7): no-inducer condition as baseline.

Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 captions state: 'Data are expressed as means (± s.d.) from three independent experiments'. Replicate counts for Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 7 and supplementary figures are not stated in the main text.
mKate/rfp fluorescence: excitation 590 nm, emission 640 nm, with OD600 normalization, in a microplate reader.

BioTek microplate reader (fluorescence/OD600 kinetics); Shimadzu ('Shimazu', Japan) spectrophotometer for OD600; Biosensor Analyzer (Jinan, China) for glucose; HPLC (Shimadzu, Japan) with refractive index detector RID-10A (Shimadzu) and Aminex HPX-87H ion exclusion column (Bio-Rad, USA); mobile phase 5 mM sulfuric acid at 1 mL/min.

Endpoint/kinetic fluorescence normalized by OD600; enzyme activity calculated from colorimetric rates under substrate-excess conditions; HPLC quantification of metabolites; data expressed as means ± s.d.; NeuAc titers expressed both as g/L and as percentage of the no-repression control; qualitative orthogonality assessment (each inducer activates only its cognate promoter). No formal statistical test (e.g., t-test/ANOVA) is reported in the main text.

Promoter screen: PrhaBAD, ParaBAD, PLtetO-1, PlacO1 showed minimal leakage (RFU 27, 31, 40, 48 uninduced) with 176.3-, 107.8-, 43.3-, 7.4-fold induction; PrhaBAD was later excluded because 10 g/L glucose abolished Rha induction; final system uses PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD (orthogonality confirmed; expression 354-4,760 RFU).
One-step three-sgRNA Golden Gate assembly: thousands of transformants in a single transformation; 5 of 7 sequenced clones carried all three sgRNAs; 2 carried only the first two.
Leaky repression: uninduced sgRNA expression caused 21.8% (PlacO1), 74.9% (PLtetO-1), 37.5% (ParaBAD) rfp reduction; induced repression reached 83.7%, 88.1%, 89.6%.

Handle mutants: mutant #3 (with PlacO1) and mutant #5 (with PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD) minimized leakage while retaining 84.5%/83% lacZ repression upon induction; Discussion states handle #5 reduced leakage inhibition of PLtetO-1/ParaBAD from 90% to 20%.
Target position effect: sgRNAs closer to the start codon repress more strongly (lacZ1, gusA1 most effective); spacer lengths 17-27 bp had no significant effect on repression (70.4-79.4%).

System characterization (MG1655RFP): without inducers only PLtetO-1 caused slight RFP decrease (22.2%); single inducer addition reduced gusA activity 48.3% (IPTG), RFP 74% (aTc), lacZ activity 32.4% (Ara); with additional inducers, repression persisted (gusA 46.5-69.5%, RFP 43.8-72.1%, lacZ 41.3-45.3%).

NeuAc application: single repression of pta, ptsI, pykA gave 126.5%, 240.8%, 144.2% of control titer; double repressions pta/ptsI 121.2%, pta/pykA 81.6%, ptsI/pykA 203.7%; triple 176%. Highest titer was ptsI single repression (2.62 g/L, ~2.4-fold vs control); ptsI/pykA 2.22 g/L; triple 1.91 g/L. Multi-gene repression was NOT superior to ptsI single repression. OD600 showed no significant changes. ptsI repression increased GlcNAc +83.2% and ManNAc +63.2%, decreased pyruvate 68%; pykA repression increased GlcNAc +11.2%, decreased pyruvate 30.9%; pta repression slightly increased pyruvate and increased acetate.
Baseline DN5/pB3 NeuAc titer (prior work, ref 30): 1.62 g/L at 48 h with ManNAc accumulation.

conflicts.topic: Best NeuAc condition framing (abstract vs Results)
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Abstract states 'the optimal combinatorial inhibition of the pta, ptsI, and pykA genes resulted in a 2.4-fold increase in NeuAc yield compared to the control' (abstract_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Results show the highest titer (2.62 g/L, 240.8% of control) was achieved by repressing ptsI ALONE; triple repression gave only 176%, and the text explicitly states 'We did not find that the combination of multi-gene repression was superior to ptsI single-gene repression' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002, _p006; Fig. 6B).
conflicts.impact: The abstract's wording implies the triple/combinatorial repression was optimal, whereas the data show single-gene ptsI repression was best; downstream users should rely on the Results/Fig. 6 data.

unsupported_values: Develop a CRISPRi-based multi-gene combinatorial repression system in Escherichia coli that uses three orthogonal low-leakage inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD) to express three sgRNAs from a single plasmid (p3gRNA-LTA), so that all repression combinations of three target genes can be assessed by adding different inducer combinations instead of constructing numerous sgRNA plasmids; demonstrate utility by optimizing NeuAc biosynthesis via repression of PEP-consuming genes (pta, ptsI, pykA).

Orthogonal low-leakage inducible promoters driving independent sgRNAs, combined with sgRNA handle mutations that reduce dCas9 affinity, will eliminate leaky repression and enable rigorous combinatorial multi-gene repression by inducer addition; reducing PEP consumption (via pta/ptsI/pykA repression) will increase NeuAc accumulation because the DN5/pB3 strain accumulates ManNAc while PEP does not, suggesting PEP is limiting.

DN5: ΔnanATEK, ΔnagEBAC, ΔldhA, ΔpoxB, ΔackA in E. coli DH5α background (constructed previously, ref 29). MG1655RFP: ΔlacI, ΔgusR, native lacZ and gusA promoters replaced by constitutive promoters, rfp integrated into genome for constitutive expression. Plasmids: p3gRNA-LTA (three-sgRNA expression plasmid with BbsI, BsaI, SapI type IIS sites between PlacO1/PLtetO-1/ParaBAD promoters and sgRNA handle sequences; optimized version uses handle mutant #3 under PlacO1 and mutant #5 under PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD); pdCas9-3TFs (dCas9 plus transcription factors lacIAM, tetR, araC); pB3 (neuB, slr1975, GNA1, feedback-resistant glmS).

CRISPR interference (CRISPRi, dCas9) with three orthogonal inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD) each expressing one sgRNA; sgRNA handle sequence mutants (#3 for PlacO1, #5 for PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD) to reduce leaky repression by lowering dCas9 affinity; a modified one-step sequential Golden Gate Assembly method (Type IIS enzymes BbsI, BsaI, SapI; T4 DNA ligase + T4 PNK; 37°C 5 min / 25°C 15 min, ten cycles per round, with sequential addition of fragments in the same reaction mixture) for rapid three-sgRNA insertion into p3gRNA-LTA; Gibson assembly for general plasmid construction; genome engineering of MG1655 (lacI/gusR knockout, promoter replacement, rfp integration) for the reporter strain.
Promoter screen: 8 candidate inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD, PrhaBAD, PCymRC, PLuxB, PsalTTC, PCin) expressing mKate, each with and without its corresponding inducer (Fig. 2A).
Orthogonality test: 4 low-leakage promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD, PrhaBAD) × 4 inducers cross-design with mKate reporter (Fig. 2B).
Glucose interference: PrhaBAD induction by Rha with 10 g/L glucose present (Figure S2).
Leakiness/repression: sgRNA targeting rfp expressed from each of the three promoters, ± inducer (Fig. 4A-C).
sgRNA handle mutant screen: 7 handle mutants (#1-#7) expressing lacZ1-targeting sgRNA from each of the three promoters, ± inducer (Fig. 4D).
Target-site position: 3 sgRNAs each targeting lacZ and gusA from ParaBAD, ± inducer (Figures S4, S5).
Spacer length: 17, 22, 24, 27 bp spacers targeting lacZ1 site (Figure S6).
System characterization: MG1655RFP with p3gRNA-LTA (gusA-, rfp-, lacZ-targeting sgRNAs) under all inducer-combination conditions (Fig. 5).

NeuAc application: DN5/pB3 with p3gRNA-LTA carrying sgRNAs targeting pta, ptsI, pykA, under all 8 inducer on/off combinations (single: pta, ptsI, pykA; double: pta/ptsI, pta/pykA, ptsI/pykA; triple: pta/ptsI/pykA; plus no-inducer control) in 48 h shake-flask fermentation (Fig. 6B, Fig. 7).
rfp repression assays: strain constitutively expressing fluorescent protein without CRISPRi (Fig. 4A caption).
Promoter screen: same promoter constructs without inducer (baseline leakage measurement, Fig. 2A red circles).
System characterization (Fig. 5): strains without sgRNA targeting any genes; control enzyme activity/fluorescence normalized to 1.
NeuAc fermentation (Fig. 6B): strains without sgRNA targeting any genes as control; titers also expressed relative to 'wildtype' (= no-repression control, 100%).
Fermentation by-product detection (Fig. 7): no-inducer condition as baseline.
LB medium, 37°C, aeration (DH5α, BW25113, MG1655).
Overnight cultures diluted 2% into 2 mL LB in 24-well plates; 37°C with high-speed shaking in BioTek microplate reader; OD600 and fluorescence every 15 min for 18 h.

Single colony into 5 mL LB + ampicillin, overnight 37°C; transferred to 50 mL LB + ampicillin at 2% inoculum for 12 h; inoculated into 50 mL fresh MTB + ampicillin + 30 g/L glucose at 4% inoculum; grown to OD600 0.4-0.6 at 30°C, 220 rpm; then 200 µM IPTG added; sampling every 6-12 h; pH maintained ~7.0 with 30% NH4OH; terminated at 48 h.
ampicillin 100 µg/mL, kanamycin 25 µg/mL, chloramphenicol 17 µg/mL, or spectinomycin 100 µg/mL as needed; Golden Gate transformants selected on LB agar with 25 µg/mL spectinomycin, overnight 37°C.

Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 captions state: 'Data are expressed as means (± s.d.) from three independent experiments'. Replicate counts for Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 7 and supplementary figures are not stated in the main text.
mKate/rfp fluorescence: excitation 590 nm, emission 640 nm, with OD600 normalization, in a microplate reader.
β-galactosidase (lacZ) activity: ONPG hydrolysis, absorbance at 420 nm (Miller-type assay adapted from OpenWetWare).
β-glucuronidase (gusA) activity: 4-NPG hydrolysis, p-nitrophenol quantified at 405 nm.
OD600 growth measurement.
Extracellular metabolite quantification (glucose, NeuAc, acetate, ethanol, formate, pyruvate, GlcNAc, ManNAc) by HPLC.
Glucose additionally measured with a biosensor analyzer.
Sanger sequencing of colonies to confirm sgRNA fragment insertion.

BioTek microplate reader (fluorescence/OD600 kinetics); Shimadzu ('Shimazu', Japan) spectrophotometer for OD600; Biosensor Analyzer (Jinan, China) for glucose; HPLC (Shimadzu, Japan) with refractive index detector RID-10A (Shimadzu) and Aminex HPX-87H ion exclusion column (Bio-Rad, USA); mobile phase 5 mM sulfuric acid at 1 mL/min.

Endpoint/kinetic fluorescence normalized by OD600; enzyme activity calculated from colorimetric rates under substrate-excess conditions; HPLC quantification of metabolites; data expressed as means ± s.d.; NeuAc titers expressed both as g/L and as percentage of the no-repression control; qualitative orthogonality assessment (each inducer activates only its cognate promoter). No formal statistical test (e.g., t-test/ANOVA) is reported in the main text.

Promoter screen: PrhaBAD, ParaBAD, PLtetO-1, PlacO1 showed minimal leakage (RFU 27, 31, 40, 48 uninduced) with 176.3-, 107.8-, 43.3-, 7.4-fold induction; PrhaBAD was later excluded because 10 g/L glucose abolished Rha induction; final system uses PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD (orthogonality confirmed; expression 354-4,760 RFU).
One-step three-sgRNA Golden Gate assembly: thousands of transformants in a single transformation; 5 of 7 sequenced clones carried all three sgRNAs; 2 carried only the first two.
Leaky repression: uninduced sgRNA expression caused 21.8% (PlacO1), 74.9% (PLtetO-1), 37.5% (ParaBAD) rfp reduction; induced repression reached 83.7%, 88.1%, 89.6%.

Handle mutants: mutant #3 (with PlacO1) and mutant #5 (with PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD) minimized leakage while retaining 84.5%/83% lacZ repression upon induction; Discussion states handle #5 reduced leakage inhibition of PLtetO-1/ParaBAD from 90% to 20%.
Target position effect: sgRNAs closer to the start codon repress more strongly (lacZ1, gusA1 most effective); spacer lengths 17-27 bp had no significant effect on repression (70.4-79.4%).

System characterization (MG1655RFP): without inducers only PLtetO-1 caused slight RFP decrease (22.2%); single inducer addition reduced gusA activity 48.3% (IPTG), RFP 74% (aTc), lacZ activity 32.4% (Ara); with additional inducers, repression persisted (gusA 46.5-69.5%, RFP 43.8-72.1%, lacZ 41.3-45.3%).

NeuAc application: single repression of pta, ptsI, pykA gave 126.5%, 240.8%, 144.2% of control titer; double repressions pta/ptsI 121.2%, pta/pykA 81.6%, ptsI/pykA 203.7%; triple 176%. Highest titer was ptsI single repression (2.62 g/L, ~2.4-fold vs control); ptsI/pykA 2.22 g/L; triple 1.91 g/L. Multi-gene repression was NOT superior to ptsI single repression. OD600 showed no significant changes. ptsI repression increased GlcNAc +83.2% and ManNAc +63.2%, decreased pyruvate 68%; pykA repression increased GlcNAc +11.2%, decreased pyruvate 30.9%; pta repression slightly increased pyruvate and increased acetate.
Baseline DN5/pB3 NeuAc titer (prior work, ref 30): 1.62 g/L at 48 h with ManNAc accumulation.

conflicts.topic: Best NeuAc condition framing (abstract vs Results)
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Abstract states 'the optimal combinatorial inhibition of the pta, ptsI, and pykA genes resulted in a 2.4-fold increase in NeuAc yield compared to the control' (abstract_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Results show the highest titer (2.62 g/L, 240.8% of control) was achieved by repressing ptsI ALONE; triple repression gave only 176%, and the text explicitly states 'We did not find that the combination of multi-gene repression was superior to ptsI single-gene repression' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002, _p006; Fig. 6B).
conflicts.impact: The abstract's wording implies the triple/combinatorial repression was optimal, whereas the data show single-gene ptsI repression was best; downstream users should rely on the Results/Fig. 6 data.

No formal statistical test (e.g., t-test/ANOVA) is reported in the main text.

value: Promoter screen: PrhaBAD, ParaBAD, PLtetO-1, PlacO1 showed minimal leakage (RFU 27, 31, 40, 48 uninduced) with 176.3-, 107.8-, 43.3-, 7.4-fold induction; PrhaBAD was later excluded because 10 g/L glucose abolished Rha induction; final system uses PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD (orthogonality confirmed; expression 354-4,760 RFU).
One-step three-sgRNA Golden Gate assembly: thousands of transformants in a single transformation; 5 of 7 sequenced clones carried all three sgRNAs; 2 carried only the first two.
Leaky repression: uninduced sgRNA expression caused 21.8% (PlacO1), 74.9% (PLtetO-1), 37.5% (ParaBAD) rfp reduction; induced repression reached 83.7%, 88.1%, 89.6%.

Handle mutants: mutant #3 (with PlacO1) and mutant #5 (with PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD) minimized leakage while retaining 84.5%/83% lacZ repression upon induction; Discussion states handle #5 reduced leakage inhibition of PLtetO-1/ParaBAD from 90% to 20%.
Target position effect: sgRNAs closer to the start codon repress more strongly (lacZ1, gusA1 most effective); spacer lengths 17-27 bp had no significant effect on repression (70.4-79.4%).

System characterization (MG1655RFP): without inducers only PLtetO-1 caused slight RFP decrease (22.2%); single inducer addition reduced gusA activity 48.3% (IPTG), RFP 74% (aTc), lacZ activity 32.4% (Ara); with additional inducers, repression persisted (gusA 46.5-69.5%, RFP 43.8-72.1%, lacZ 41.3-45.3%).

NeuAc application: single repression of pta, ptsI, pykA gave 126.5%, 240.8%, 144.2% of control titer; double repressions pta/ptsI 121.2%, pta/pykA 81.6%, ptsI/pykA 203.7%; triple 176%. Highest titer was ptsI single repression (2.62 g/L, ~2.4-fold vs control); ptsI/pykA 2.22 g/L; triple 1.91 g/L. Multi-gene repression was NOT superior to ptsI single repression. OD600 showed no significant changes. ptsI repression increased GlcNAc +83.2% and ManNAc +63.2%, decreased pyruvate 68%; pykA repression increased GlcNAc +11.2%, decreased pyruvate 30.9%; pta repression slightly increased pyruvate and increased acetate.
Baseline DN5/pB3 NeuAc titer (prior work, ref 30): 1.62 g/L at 48 h with ManNAc accumulation.
outcomes.notes: The 2.4-fold increase in the abstract corresponds to the ptsI single-repression condition (240.8%, 2.62 g/L), which the abstract loosely calls 'optimal combinatorial inhibition of pta, ptsI, and pykA' — a mild internal wording tension (see conflicts). DN5/pB3 baseline 1.62 g/L is from prior work (ref 30), attribution: background_citation for the titer value, though the same strain is reused here.

experiments.purpose: Identify inducible promoters with high induced expression and low background leakage for sgRNA expression.
experiments.host: E. coli BW25113 or MG1655 (characterization hosts; exact host for this screen not specified per-experiment in main text)
experiments.intervention: Expression of mKate reporter from 8 candidate inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD, PrhaBAD, PCymRC, PLuxB, PsalTTC, PCin), each ± its inducer.
experiments.conditions: LB, 24-well plates, 2 mL, 37°C, high-speed shaking, 18 h; inducer doses per Fig. 2 caption (0.5 mM IPTG, 4.3 µM aTc, 13.3 mM Ara, 121.8 µM Rha, 100 µM Cuma, 10 µM OC6, 100 µM Sal, 10 µM OHC14).
experiments.control: Same promoter constructs without inducer (uninduced baseline).
experiments.readout: mKate fluorescence (ex 590/em 640) and OD600 every 15 min for 18 h.
experiments.analysis: Induced vs uninduced fluorescence intensities; fold-change calculation.
experiments.outcome: PrhaBAD, ParaBAD, PLtetO-1, PlacO1 selected for low leakage; PrhaBAD later excluded due to glucose repression of induction (10 g/L glucose).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (deliberate selection and adoption of specific promoters as system components), Q2 pass (characterization performed in this study), Q3 pass (selection determined the final system composition and excluded PrhaBAD for glucose-based fermentations).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Building an inducer-controlled regulation layer (orthogonal inducible promoters) to dynamically control target gene expression; closest category is M7 动态调控.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Eight candidate promoters showed varying induced intensity and leakage; high-leakage promoters would cause undesired repression because sgRNA is functional immediately upon transcription.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Direct experimental fluorescence measurements of all eight promoters with and without inducers.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The three final promoters were chosen from an empirical screen of eight candidates based on measured leakage/orthogonality, not from a stated mechanistic prediction; PrhaBAD exclusion was driven by the measured glucose effect.
alternatives_considered: PrhaBAD: highest induction fold (176.3x) and low leakage, but Rha induction was abolished by 10 g/L glucose, so excluded for glucose-based fermentation.
PLuxB, PCin, PsalTTC, PCymRC: high induced expression but significant background leakage, excluded.

experiments.purpose: Enable rapid construction of a three-sgRNA expression plasmid (p3gRNA-LTA) without building separate plasmids per combination.
experiments.intervention: Modified one-step sequential Golden Gate Assembly: three sgRNA insertion sites flanked by paired Type IIS sites (BbsI, BsaI, SapI) between promoters and handle sequences; annealed oligo spacers sequentially ligated in one reaction mixture (10 cycles of 37°C 5 min / 25°C 15 min per round).
experiments.conditions: 20 µL reaction with defined enzyme/reagent amounts; transformants selected on LB + 25 µg/mL spectinomycin, overnight 37°C.
experiments.control: not_applicable (method development; no experimental control group)
experiments.replicates: Single transformation yielding thousands of colonies; 7 clones randomly picked for sequencing.
experiments.readout: Colony count; Sanger sequencing of 7 clones.
experiments.analysis: Fraction of sequenced clones containing all three sgRNAs.
experiments.outcome: 5/7 clones contained all three sgRNAs; 2/7 contained only the first two (last one omitted).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (new assembly method designed and implemented), Q2 pass (developed here), Q3 pass (this method is the enabling step for all subsequent spacer swapping).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Method enabling rapid construction/screening of sgRNA combinations — an integrated construction-and-screening enabling tool.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Conventional combinatorial CRISPRi requires constructing a large number of sgRNA plasmids (e.g., 7 plasmids for all combinations of 3 genes; 25 for 4 genes), which is labor-intensive.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Assembly success directly verified by sequencing of 7 clones.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicitly described as a modification of the published Golden Gate Assembly method (Engler et al., ref 22), adapted to sequential one-pot ligation of three spacers.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When constructing multi-sgRNA CRISPRi plasmids for combinatorial repression in E. coli, apply a one-pot sequential Golden Gate strategy with distinct Type IIS sites (BbsI/BsaI/SapI) per insertion site, because it yields correct three-spacer assemblies in a single transformation (5/7 verified clones) without intermediate purification.

experiments.purpose: Quantify leaky repression of the three promoters when driving sgRNA and mitigate it by mutating the sgRNA handle sequence to reduce dCas9 affinity.
experiments.host: E. coli characterization host (BW25113/MG1655; exact per-assay host not specified in main text)
experiments.intervention: sgRNA targeting rfp expressed from each of the three promoters ± inducer; then seven sgRNA handle mutants (#1-#7, selected from Reis et al. ref 28 set) screened with lacZ1 spacer targeting lacZ from each promoter.
experiments.conditions: LB, 24-well plates, 18 h, 37°C; inducers 0.5 mM IPTG / 4.3 µM aTc / 13.3 mM Ara.
experiments.control: Strain constitutively expressing fluorescent protein without CRISPRi (Fig. 4A); uninduced cultures as leakage baseline.
experiments.readout: rfp fluorescence; lacZ β-galactosidase activity (ONPG, A420).
experiments.analysis: Percent fluorescence/activity reduction relative to control, ± inducer.
experiments.outcome: Leakage of 21.8%/74.9%/37.5% (PlacO1/PLtetO-1/ParaBAD) on rfp; handle mutant #3 chosen for PlacO1 (84.5% induced repression, near-intact uninduced lacZ), mutant #5 for PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD (balance of low leakage and repression; leakage inhibition reduced from ~90% to ~20% per Discussion).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (deliberate handle-sequence mutation adopted into the final p3gRNA-LTA), Q2 pass (screen performed here), Q3 pass (mutant choice defined the final system configuration).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Tuning the dynamic regulation layer (reducing leaky CRISPRi repression) — component engineering within the control system.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Uninduced sgRNA expression from all three promoters caused substantial reporter repression (up to 74.9%), which would confound combinatorial repression.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Experimentally measured lacZ activity for each handle mutant ± inducer (Fig. 4D).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The paper explicitly states that handle mutations with different repression intensities and reduced dCas9 affinity were reported by Reis et al. [28], and the authors hypothesized these would reduce leakage; a mechanistic rationale (lower dCas9 affinity reduces repression at basal sgRNA levels) is also given in the Discussion, so both tags apply.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When inducible-promoter-driven CRISPRi in E. coli shows unacceptable leaky repression, apply sgRNA handle mutations that modestly reduce dCas9 affinity, because basal-level sgRNA then falls below the functional threshold while induced levels retain strong repression (validated for lacZ/rfp reporters and three promoters in this study).
alternatives_considered: crRNA mismatch strategy, decoy crRNA binding sites, and feedback control of crRNA expression (Van Hove et al., ref 42) — cited as prior approaches; the handle-mutation route was chosen because it requires only inserting a 20 bp targeting sequence with no additional design.

experiments.purpose: Assess how sgRNA targeting position and spacer length affect repression.
experiments.intervention: Three sgRNAs each targeting lacZ and gusA expressed from ParaBAD; four spacer lengths (17, 22, 24, 27 bp) targeting the lacZ1 site.
experiments.conditions: LB, 18 h induction, 37°C.
experiments.readout: lacZ/gusA enzyme activity.
experiments.analysis: Percent repression per target site / spacer length.
experiments.outcome: Sites closer to the start codon repress more strongly (lacZ1, gusA1 best); 17-27 bp spacer length had no significant effect (70.4-79.4% repression).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fail/Q3 fail: a characterization of design parameters (target position, spacer length) without a new engineering modification adopted as a system change; it validates design heuristics for sgRNA choice rather than constituting a new build decision.

experiments.purpose: Characterize the optimized combinatorial repression system on three independent reporter genes in one strain.
experiments.host: E. coli MG1655RFP (ΔlacI, ΔgusR, constitutive lacZ and gusA promoters, genomically integrated constitutive rfp)
experiments.intervention: p3gRNA-LTA carrying sgRNAs targeting gusA (PlacO1), rfp (PLtetO-1), lacZ (ParaBAD); all inducer combinations applied.
experiments.conditions: LB, 24-well plates, 18 h, 37°C; single and combined inducers.
experiments.control: Strains without sgRNA targeting any genes; control values normalized to 1.
experiments.replicates: three independent experiments (means ± s.d.); replicate type beyond 'independent experiments' not further defined
experiments.readout: gusA activity, RFP fluorescence, lacZ activity.
experiments.analysis: Percent inhibition under each inducer combination relative to control.
experiments.outcome: Independent and combinatorial repression achieved; residual cross-condition repression ranged 41.3-74%; only PLtetO-1 showed slight leak (22.2% RFP decrease uninduced).

experiments.purpose: Apply the combinatorial repression system to optimize NeuAc biosynthesis by repressing PEP-consuming genes.
experiments.host: E. coli DN5/pB3 (DN5: ΔnanATEK ΔnagEBAC ΔldhA ΔpoxB ΔackA in DH5α background, from prior work ref 29; pB3 carries neuB, slr1975, GNA1, feedback-resistant glmS)
experiments.intervention: CRISPRi repression of pta, ptsI, pykA via p3gRNA-LTA (PlacO1→sgRNA-pta, PLtetO-1→sgRNA-ptsI, ParaBAD→sgRNA-pykA); all 7 on/off inducer combinations plus no-inducer control, set by inducer addition rather than separate plasmids.
experiments.conditions: Shake-flask batch fermentation: MTB + 30 g/L glucose + ampicillin, 30°C, 220 rpm, 48 h, pH ~7.0 maintained with 30% NH4OH; inducers added at transfer to shake flask; 200 µM IPTG at OD600 0.4-0.6 (generic fermentation protocol).
experiments.control: Strain without sgRNA targeting any genes (titers expressed as % of this control).
experiments.readout: NeuAc titer (HPLC), OD600, by-products (glucose, acetate, ethanol, formate, pyruvate, GlcNAc, ManNAc).
experiments.analysis: Titers as g/L and % of control; by-product concentration changes.
experiments.outcome: ptsI single repression gave the highest titer (2.62 g/L, 240.8% of control ≈ 2.4-fold); ptsI/pykA 2.22 g/L; triple repression 1.91 g/L; pta/pykA decreased titer (81.6%). Combinatorial repression was not superior to ptsI single repression. ptsI repression raised GlcNAc (+83.2%) and ManNAc (+63.2%) and lowered pyruvate (−68%); no significant OD600 change.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (deliberate CRISPRi repression of three PEP-consuming genes), Q2 pass (this repression experiment is new in this study, although the DN5/pB3 chassis itself is background from refs 29-30), Q3 pass (the comparison across combinations identified ptsI single repression as optimal and revealed that more repression is not better, informing future flux-tuning strategy).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Blocking competing PEP-consumption pathways (pyruvate kinase pykA, PTS ptsI, phosphotransacetylase pta) to redirect PEP flux toward NeuAc synthesis — competitive/bypass flux blocking.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: DN5/pB3 accumulated large amounts of ManNAc (direct NeuAc precursor) while PEP showed no obvious accumulation, suggesting PEP supply was limiting relative to ManNAc.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Trigger is the measured metabolite accumulation profile of DN5/pB3 (ManNAc accumulation, no PEP accumulation), and the intervention outcome was measured by HPLC titers.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The paper explicitly reasons from precursor imbalance (ManNAc accumulates, PEP does not) to a mechanistic hypothesis that PEP consumption limits NeuAc synthesis, and selects the three genes as the main PEP-depleting routes (acetyl-CoA via pyruvate, PTS energy coupling).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a NeuAc-producing E. coli chassis accumulates the ManNAc branch precursor but not PEP, apply CRISPRi repression of PEP-consuming genes (ptsI, pykA, pta) — with ptsI repression as the priority single target — because redirecting PEP away from the PTS and pyruvate increases precursor supply for NeuAc (validated for NeuAc production in E. coli DN5 background).
alternatives_considered: Full combinatorial repression of all three genes was tested but abandoned as optimal: triple repression (1.91 g/L) and pta/pykA (81.6%) underperformed ptsI single repression (2.62 g/L), showing stronger/wider repression is not necessarily better.

conflicts.topic: Best NeuAc condition framing (abstract vs Results)
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Abstract states 'the optimal combinatorial inhibition of the pta, ptsI, and pykA genes resulted in a 2.4-fold increase in NeuAc yield compared to the control' (abstract_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Results show the highest titer (2.62 g/L, 240.8% of control) was achieved by repressing ptsI ALONE; triple repression gave only 176%, and the text explicitly states 'We did not find that the combination of multi-gene repression was superior to ptsI single-gene repression' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002, _p006; Fig. 6B).
conflicts.impact: The abstract's wording implies the triple/combinatorial repression was optimal, whereas the data show single-gene ptsI repression was best; downstream users should rely on the Results/Fig. 6 data.

conflicts.topic: Inducer addition protocol for combinatorial fermentation
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Batch fermentation method adds 200 µM IPTG at OD600 0.4-0.6 (batch_fermentation_of_neuac_p001).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Fig. 6 caption states different combinations of inducers were added when the strain was transferred to the shake flask (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p005).
conflicts.impact: Timing and composition of inducer addition (transfer-time vs mid-exponential; whether aTc/Ara were co-added with IPTG) cannot be unambiguously reconstructed from the main text; exact reproduction requires clarification or supplement.

conflicts.topic: Use of 'wildtype' for the NeuAc control
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Results express titers as percentage of 'the wildtype' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Fig. 6 caption defines the control as 'strains without sgRNA targeting any genes', i.e., the engineered DN5/pB3 host carrying the plasmid without targeting spacers — not a natural wild type.
conflicts.impact: Terminology only; extraction records the control as a non-targeting-plasmid control in the DN5/pB3 background.

conflicts.prose_interpretation: Text describes pykA as 'encoding pyruvate carboxykinase' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: In standard E. coli nomenclature pykA encodes pyruvate kinase II; the paper's own pathway logic (PEP→pyruvate conversion) is consistent with pyruvate kinase activity.
conflicts.impact: Likely an author wording error; gene identity (pykA) is unambiguous, so extraction retains pykA as the target with the paper's functional role (PEP to pyruvate conversion).

objective.value: Develop a CRISPRi-based multi-gene combinatorial repression system in Escherichia coli that uses three orthogonal low-leakage inducible promoters (PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD) to express three sgRNAs from a single plasmid (p3gRNA-LTA), so that all repression combinations of three target genes can be assessed by adding different inducer combinations instead of constructing numerous sgRNA plasmids; demonstrate utility by optimizing NeuAc biosynthesis via repression of PEP-consuming genes (pta, ptsI, pykA).
objective.notes: Primary goal is a methods/platform contribution (combinatorial repression system) demonstrated with a metabolic engineering application (NeuAc).

hypothesis.value: Orthogonal low-leakage inducible promoters driving independent sgRNAs, combined with sgRNA handle mutations that reduce dCas9 affinity, will eliminate leaky repression and enable rigorous combinatorial multi-gene repression by inducer addition; reducing PEP consumption (via pta/ptsI/pykA repression) will increase NeuAc accumulation because the DN5/pB3 strain accumulates ManNAc while PEP does not, suggesting PEP is limiting.
hypothesis.notes: The PEP-limitation hypothesis is stated from observed ManNAc accumulation without PEP accumulation; the handle-mutation hypothesis is attributed to prior literature (Reis et al., ref 28) plus the authors' hypothesis.

value: Promoter screen: PrhaBAD, ParaBAD, PLtetO-1, PlacO1 showed minimal leakage (RFU 27, 31, 40, 48 uninduced) with 176.3-, 107.8-, 43.3-, 7.4-fold induction; PrhaBAD was later excluded because 10 g/L glucose abolished Rha induction; final system uses PlacO1, PLtetO-1, ParaBAD (orthogonality confirmed; expression 354-4,760 RFU).
One-step three-sgRNA Golden Gate assembly: thousands of transformants in a single transformation; 5 of 7 sequenced clones carried all three sgRNAs; 2 carried only the first two.
Leaky repression: uninduced sgRNA expression caused 21.8% (PlacO1), 74.9% (PLtetO-1), 37.5% (ParaBAD) rfp reduction; induced repression reached 83.7%, 88.1%, 89.6%.

Handle mutants: mutant #3 (with PlacO1) and mutant #5 (with PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD) minimized leakage while retaining 84.5%/83% lacZ repression upon induction; Discussion states handle #5 reduced leakage inhibition of PLtetO-1/ParaBAD from 90% to 20%.
Target position effect: sgRNAs closer to the start codon repress more strongly (lacZ1, gusA1 most effective); spacer lengths 17-27 bp had no significant effect on repression (70.4-79.4%).

System characterization (MG1655RFP): without inducers only PLtetO-1 caused slight RFP decrease (22.2%); single inducer addition reduced gusA activity 48.3% (IPTG), RFP 74% (aTc), lacZ activity 32.4% (Ara); with additional inducers, repression persisted (gusA 46.5-69.5%, RFP 43.8-72.1%, lacZ 41.3-45.3%).

NeuAc application: single repression of pta, ptsI, pykA gave 126.5%, 240.8%, 144.2% of control titer; double repressions pta/ptsI 121.2%, pta/pykA 81.6%, ptsI/pykA 203.7%; triple 176%. Highest titer was ptsI single repression (2.62 g/L, ~2.4-fold vs control); ptsI/pykA 2.22 g/L; triple 1.91 g/L. Multi-gene repression was NOT superior to ptsI single repression. OD600 showed no significant changes. ptsI repression increased GlcNAc +83.2% and ManNAc +63.2%, decreased pyruvate 68%; pykA repression increased GlcNAc +11.2%, decreased pyruvate 30.9%; pta repression slightly increased pyruvate and increased acetate.
Baseline DN5/pB3 NeuAc titer (prior work, ref 30): 1.62 g/L at 48 h with ManNAc accumulation.
outcomes.notes: The 2.4-fold increase in the abstract corresponds to the ptsI single-repression condition (240.8%, 2.62 g/L), which the abstract loosely calls 'optimal combinatorial inhibition of pta, ptsI, and pykA' — a mild internal wording tension (see conflicts). DN5/pB3 baseline 1.62 g/L is from prior work (ref 30), attribution: background_citation for the titer value, though the same strain is reused here.

experiments.conditions: LB, 24-well plates, 2 mL, 37°C, high-speed shaking, 18 h; inducer doses per Fig. 2 caption (0.5 mM IPTG, 4.3 µM aTc, 13.3 mM Ara, 121.8 µM Rha, 100 µM Cuma, 10 µM OC6, 100 µM Sal, 10 µM OHC14).
experiments.control: Same promoter constructs without inducer (uninduced baseline).

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Building an inducer-controlled regulation layer (orthogonal inducible promoters) to dynamically control target gene expression; closest category is M7 动态调控.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Eight candidate promoters showed varying induced intensity and leakage; high-leakage promoters would cause undesired repression because sgRNA is functional immediately upon transcription.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Direct experimental fluorescence measurements of all eight promoters with and without inducers.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The three final promoters were chosen from an empirical screen of eight candidates based on measured leakage/orthogonality, not from a stated mechanistic prediction; PrhaBAD exclusion was driven by the measured glucose effect.
alternatives_considered: PrhaBAD: highest induction fold (176.3x) and low leakage, but Rha induction was abolished by 10 g/L glucose, so excluded for glucose-based fermentation.
PLuxB, PCin, PsalTTC, PCymRC: high induced expression but significant background leakage, excluded.

experiments.purpose: Enable rapid construction of a three-sgRNA expression plasmid (p3gRNA-LTA) without building separate plasmids per combination.
experiments.intervention: Modified one-step sequential Golden Gate Assembly: three sgRNA insertion sites flanked by paired Type IIS sites (BbsI, BsaI, SapI) between promoters and handle sequences; annealed oligo spacers sequentially ligated in one reaction mixture (10 cycles of 37°C 5 min / 25°C 15 min per round).
experiments.conditions: 20 µL reaction with defined enzyme/reagent amounts; transformants selected on LB + 25 µg/mL spectinomycin, overnight 37°C.
experiments.control: not_applicable (method development; no experimental control group)
experiments.replicates: Single transformation yielding thousands of colonies; 7 clones randomly picked for sequencing.
experiments.readout: Colony count; Sanger sequencing of 7 clones.
experiments.analysis: Fraction of sequenced clones containing all three sgRNAs.
experiments.outcome: 5/7 clones contained all three sgRNAs; 2/7 contained only the first two (last one omitted).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (new assembly method designed and implemented), Q2 pass (developed here), Q3 pass (this method is the enabling step for all subsequent spacer swapping).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Method enabling rapid construction/screening of sgRNA combinations — an integrated construction-and-screening enabling tool.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Conventional combinatorial CRISPRi requires constructing a large number of sgRNA plasmids (e.g., 7 plasmids for all combinations of 3 genes; 25 for 4 genes), which is labor-intensive.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Assembly success directly verified by sequencing of 7 clones.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicitly described as a modification of the published Golden Gate Assembly method (Engler et al., ref 22), adapted to sequential one-pot ligation of three spacers.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When constructing multi-sgRNA CRISPRi plasmids for combinatorial repression in E. coli, apply a one-pot sequential Golden Gate strategy with distinct Type IIS sites (BbsI/BsaI/SapI) per insertion site, because it yields correct three-spacer assemblies in a single transformation (5/7 verified clones) without intermediate purification.

experiments.purpose: Quantify leaky repression of the three promoters when driving sgRNA and mitigate it by mutating the sgRNA handle sequence to reduce dCas9 affinity.
experiments.host: E. coli characterization host (BW25113/MG1655; exact per-assay host not specified in main text)
experiments.intervention: sgRNA targeting rfp expressed from each of the three promoters ± inducer; then seven sgRNA handle mutants (#1-#7, selected from Reis et al. ref 28 set) screened with lacZ1 spacer targeting lacZ from each promoter.
experiments.conditions: LB, 24-well plates, 18 h, 37°C; inducers 0.5 mM IPTG / 4.3 µM aTc / 13.3 mM Ara.
experiments.control: Strain constitutively expressing fluorescent protein without CRISPRi (Fig. 4A); uninduced cultures as leakage baseline.
experiments.readout: rfp fluorescence; lacZ β-galactosidase activity (ONPG, A420).
experiments.analysis: Percent fluorescence/activity reduction relative to control, ± inducer.
experiments.outcome: Leakage of 21.8%/74.9%/37.5% (PlacO1/PLtetO-1/ParaBAD) on rfp; handle mutant #3 chosen for PlacO1 (84.5% induced repression, near-intact uninduced lacZ), mutant #5 for PLtetO-1 and ParaBAD (balance of low leakage and repression; leakage inhibition reduced from ~90% to ~20% per Discussion).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (deliberate handle-sequence mutation adopted into the final p3gRNA-LTA), Q2 pass (screen performed here), Q3 pass (mutant choice defined the final system configuration).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Tuning the dynamic regulation layer (reducing leaky CRISPRi repression) — component engineering within the control system.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Uninduced sgRNA expression from all three promoters caused substantial reporter repression (up to 74.9%), which would confound combinatorial repression.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Experimentally measured lacZ activity for each handle mutant ± inducer (Fig. 4D).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The paper explicitly states that handle mutations with different repression intensities and reduced dCas9 affinity were reported by Reis et al. [28], and the authors hypothesized these would reduce leakage; a mechanistic rationale (lower dCas9 affinity reduces repression at basal sgRNA levels) is also given in the Discussion, so both tags apply.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When inducible-promoter-driven CRISPRi in E. coli shows unacceptable leaky repression, apply sgRNA handle mutations that modestly reduce dCas9 affinity, because basal-level sgRNA then falls below the functional threshold while induced levels retain strong repression (validated for lacZ/rfp reporters and three promoters in this study).
alternatives_considered: crRNA mismatch strategy, decoy crRNA binding sites, and feedback control of crRNA expression (Van Hove et al., ref 42) — cited as prior approaches; the handle-mutation route was chosen because it requires only inserting a 20 bp targeting sequence with no additional design.

experiments.purpose: Assess how sgRNA targeting position and spacer length affect repression.
experiments.intervention: Three sgRNAs each targeting lacZ and gusA expressed from ParaBAD; four spacer lengths (17, 22, 24, 27 bp) targeting the lacZ1 site.
experiments.conditions: LB, 18 h induction, 37°C.
experiments.readout: lacZ/gusA enzyme activity.
experiments.analysis: Percent repression per target site / spacer length.
experiments.outcome: Sites closer to the start codon repress more strongly (lacZ1, gusA1 best); 17-27 bp spacer length had no significant effect (70.4-79.4% repression).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fail/Q3 fail: a characterization of design parameters (target position, spacer length) without a new engineering modification adopted as a system change; it validates design heuristics for sgRNA choice rather than constituting a new build decision.

experiments.intervention: p3gRNA-LTA carrying sgRNAs targeting gusA (PlacO1), rfp (PLtetO-1), lacZ (ParaBAD); all inducer combinations applied.
experiments.conditions: LB, 24-well plates, 18 h, 37°C; single and combined inducers.
experiments.control: Strains without sgRNA targeting any genes; control values normalized to 1.

experiments.readout: gusA activity, RFP fluorescence, lacZ activity.

experiments.purpose: Apply the combinatorial repression system to optimize NeuAc biosynthesis by repressing PEP-consuming genes.
experiments.host: E. coli DN5/pB3 (DN5: ΔnanATEK ΔnagEBAC ΔldhA ΔpoxB ΔackA in DH5α background, from prior work ref 29; pB3 carries neuB, slr1975, GNA1, feedback-resistant glmS)
experiments.intervention: CRISPRi repression of pta, ptsI, pykA via p3gRNA-LTA (PlacO1→sgRNA-pta, PLtetO-1→sgRNA-ptsI, ParaBAD→sgRNA-pykA); all 7 on/off inducer combinations plus no-inducer control, set by inducer addition rather than separate plasmids.
experiments.conditions: Shake-flask batch fermentation: MTB + 30 g/L glucose + ampicillin, 30°C, 220 rpm, 48 h, pH ~7.0 maintained with 30% NH4OH; inducers added at transfer to shake flask; 200 µM IPTG at OD600 0.4-0.6 (generic fermentation protocol).
experiments.control: Strain without sgRNA targeting any genes (titers expressed as % of this control).
experiments.readout: NeuAc titer (HPLC), OD600, by-products (glucose, acetate, ethanol, formate, pyruvate, GlcNAc, ManNAc).
experiments.analysis: Titers as g/L and % of control; by-product concentration changes.
experiments.outcome: ptsI single repression gave the highest titer (2.62 g/L, 240.8% of control ≈ 2.4-fold); ptsI/pykA 2.22 g/L; triple repression 1.91 g/L; pta/pykA decreased titer (81.6%). Combinatorial repression was not superior to ptsI single repression. ptsI repression raised GlcNAc (+83.2%) and ManNAc (+63.2%) and lowered pyruvate (−68%); no significant OD600 change.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (deliberate CRISPRi repression of three PEP-consuming genes), Q2 pass (this repression experiment is new in this study, although the DN5/pB3 chassis itself is background from refs 29-30), Q3 pass (the comparison across combinations identified ptsI single repression as optimal and revealed that more repression is not better, informing future flux-tuning strategy).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Blocking competing PEP-consumption pathways (pyruvate kinase pykA, PTS ptsI, phosphotransacetylase pta) to redirect PEP flux toward NeuAc synthesis — competitive/bypass flux blocking.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: DN5/pB3 accumulated large amounts of ManNAc (direct NeuAc precursor) while PEP showed no obvious accumulation, suggesting PEP supply was limiting relative to ManNAc.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Trigger is the measured metabolite accumulation profile of DN5/pB3 (ManNAc accumulation, no PEP accumulation), and the intervention outcome was measured by HPLC titers.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The paper explicitly reasons from precursor imbalance (ManNAc accumulates, PEP does not) to a mechanistic hypothesis that PEP consumption limits NeuAc synthesis, and selects the three genes as the main PEP-depleting routes (acetyl-CoA via pyruvate, PTS energy coupling).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a NeuAc-producing E. coli chassis accumulates the ManNAc branch precursor but not PEP, apply CRISPRi repression of PEP-consuming genes (ptsI, pykA, pta) — with ptsI repression as the priority single target — because redirecting PEP away from the PTS and pyruvate increases precursor supply for NeuAc (validated for NeuAc production in E. coli DN5 background).
alternatives_considered: Full combinatorial repression of all three genes was tested but abandoned as optimal: triple repression (1.91 g/L) and pta/pykA (81.6%) underperformed ptsI single repression (2.62 g/L), showing stronger/wider repression is not necessarily better.

conflicts.topic: Best NeuAc condition framing (abstract vs Results)
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Abstract states 'the optimal combinatorial inhibition of the pta, ptsI, and pykA genes resulted in a 2.4-fold increase in NeuAc yield compared to the control' (abstract_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Results show the highest titer (2.62 g/L, 240.8% of control) was achieved by repressing ptsI ALONE; triple repression gave only 176%, and the text explicitly states 'We did not find that the combination of multi-gene repression was superior to ptsI single-gene repression' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002, _p006; Fig. 6B).
conflicts.impact: The abstract's wording implies the triple/combinatorial repression was optimal, whereas the data show single-gene ptsI repression was best; downstream users should rely on the Results/Fig. 6 data.

conflicts.topic: Inducer addition protocol for combinatorial fermentation
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Batch fermentation method adds 200 µM IPTG at OD600 0.4-0.6 (batch_fermentation_of_neuac_p001).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Fig. 6 caption states different combinations of inducers were added when the strain was transferred to the shake flask (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p005).
conflicts.impact: Timing and composition of inducer addition (transfer-time vs mid-exponential; whether aTc/Ara were co-added with IPTG) cannot be unambiguously reconstructed from the main text; exact reproduction requires clarification or supplement.

conflicts.topic: Use of 'wildtype' for the NeuAc control
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Results express titers as percentage of 'the wildtype' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Fig. 6 caption defines the control as 'strains without sgRNA targeting any genes', i.e., the engineered DN5/pB3 host carrying the plasmid without targeting spacers — not a natural wild type.
conflicts.impact: Terminology only; extraction records the control as a non-targeting-plasmid control in the DN5/pB3 background.

conflicts.prose_interpretation: Text describes pykA as 'encoding pyruvate carboxykinase' (optimization_of_the_biosynthesis_pathway_of_neuac_p002).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: In standard E. coli nomenclature pykA encodes pyruvate kinase II; the paper's own pathway logic (PEP→pyruvate conversion) is consistent with pyruvate kinase activity.
conflicts.impact: Likely an author wording error; gene identity (pykA) is unambiguous, so extraction retains pykA as the target with the paper's functional role (PEP to pyruvate conversion).

unsupported_values: Construct an Escherichia coli W derivative with improved gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) production from glycerol by combining adaptive laboratory evolution (1300 generations under glycerol limitation) with rational metabolic engineering (deletion of ackA, mgsA, gabT), and decipher the molecular basis of glycerol adaptation (mutation profiling, enzyme kinetics, transcriptomics).

ALE-improved glycerol uptake/utilization translates into superior growth-coupled GABA production, and redirecting acetate-overflow flux while blocking the methylglyoxal bypass and the GABA shunt in the evolved background further increases GABA titer and productivity.

Escherichia coli W (parental wild-type; reference genome NC_017635.1; ATCC 9637 per cited Archer et al. 2011); glycerol-evolved single clone CY02; reverse-engineered single mutants glpK^m and crp^m, double mutant glpK^m crp^m, and reverse-engineered mglC mutant; CY02 knockout derivatives CY02_ΔackA, CY02_ΔgabT, CY02_ΔmgsA, double KOs (ΔgabTΔackA, ΔgabTΔmgsA, ΔmgsAΔackA) and CY02_TKO; wild-type lacZ:mtGAD strain and its knockout derivatives; E. coli BL21(DE3) used only as GlpK overexpression host.

CY02 carries 28 new mutations vs the lab parental stock, including glpK 707G>A (Thr235Met, glpK^m), crp SNV (Arg209His, crp^m), ptsP 522InsT (Pro174fs), rsfS 19G>C (Gln6*), mglC 15Adel (Asn4fs); engineered knockouts ΔackA, ΔmgsA, ΔgabT constructed singly, as doubles, and as triple (CY02_TKO); GABA production cassette = chromosomal insertion of mutant glutamate decarboxylase B (mtGAD) under promoter PLtetQ-1 at the lacZ locus (constitutive in E. coli W, which lacks the cognate repressor), marker-free.

Serial-batch ALE in M9-glycerol with 12 h transfers and stepwise reduction of initial OD600 (0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016) for 1300 generations; single-clone isolation on M9-glycerol agar; whole-genome resequencing (Illumina MiSeq 50-cycle SE); lambda-Red recombineering for point-mutation reverse engineering and KanR-mediated gene deletion (pKD13/pKD46/pCP20, marker cured at 42 C); chromosomal insertion of mtGAD cassette; GlpK overexpression/purification (pET28a, BL21(DE3), Ni-NTA) and coupled-enzyme kinetic assays; RNA-seq + DESeq2; RT-qPCR; intracellular cAMP ELISA; HPLC quantification of GABA/glycerol; Cedex Bio Analyzer glycerol/acetate assays.

Per experiment: (ALE) single evolving lineage + parental reference; (fitness/GUR, Fig. 2A/B) parental WT, glpK^m, crp^m, glpK^m crp^m, CY02; (enzyme kinetics) purified WT GlpK vs GlpK T235M; (cAMP, Fig. 3B) WT, three reverse-engineered mutants, CY02; (RNA-seq) WT vs CY02; (acetate, Fig. 4B) same five strains; (minimal-medium GABA) WT vs CY02; (stationary-phase GABA screen) WT, glpK^m, crp^m, glpK^m crp^m, CY02; (time-course) WT vs CY02; (knockout, Fig. 6) CY02 + 3 singles + 3 doubles + TKO, and in parallel WT lacZ:mtGAD + its single/double/triple KO derivatives.

Parental E. coli W wild-type as baseline control in every phenotypic, enzymatic, transcriptomic and production comparison; wild-type GlpK (GlpK^w) as enzyme control; wild-type lacZ:mtGAD strain as background control to test whether knockout benefits are intrinsic or specific to the evolved CY02 background; no exogenous positive control reported.

37 C, 200 rpm, 50 mL culture in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks (growth, glycerol/acetate/GABA measurements); ALE: same flask format with transfer to fresh M9-glycerol every 12 h, initial OD600 stepped 0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016; growth-rate screen (Fig. S7): 96-well EPOCH2 plate reader, 37 C, 807 rpm double-orbital, 110 uL working volume, OD600 every 10 min for 24 h; exponential-phase sampling for cAMP (OD not specified) and RNA-seq at OD600 0.4-0.5.

M9 minimal medium (BD) + 0.2% (v/v) glycerol as sole carbon source (ALE, fitness, GUR, acetate); M9 + 0.2% (v/v) glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract for minimal-medium GABA production; LB + 2% (v/v) pure glycerol for optimized GABA production; M9 + 2 g/L glycerol for RNA-seq cultures; LB + kanamycin 50 ug/mL for mutant selection and BL21(DE3) expression.

Glycerol: 0.2% (v/v) in minimal medium; 2% (v/v) in LB production medium (optimum from growth-rate screen); 2 g/L for RNA-seq cultures; yeast extract 50 mg/L; kanamycin 50 ug/mL; IPTG 1 mM for GlpK induction; recombinogenic DNA 1 ug per electroporation; no chemical inducer needed for mtGAD (constitutive).

ALE: 1300 generations, serial transfer every 12 h; growth profiles sampled every 2 h; plate-reader screen 24 h; GABA time-course over 24 h; glycerol/acetate samples at 1 h intervals during exponential phase after 1.5 h initial incubation; RNA-seq harvest at OD600 0.4-0.5; stationary-phase GABA endpoint measurements.

Biological duplicates: specific growth rate, GUR (Fig. 2A/B) and acetate secretion (Fig. 4B). Biological triplicates: cAMP (each measured in technical duplicates), RNA-seq (high correlation among triplicates), GABA/glycerol time-courses in Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 (stated as three biological triplicates / biological triplicates). Enzyme specific activity: six replicates (WT GlpK) and five replicates (GlpK T235M), replicate type not defined. RT-qPCR: two biological replicates x three technical replicates. ALE: a single evolving lineage; single endpoint clone analyzed.

OD600 growth measurement; glycerol consumption and acetate secretion rates via Cedex Bio Analyzer (Glycerol Bio Test / Acetate V2 kits) with rate equations r=mu/Y; GABA by HPLC-UV - Primesep 100 column (20 mM phosphoric acid/ACN 80/20, 215 nm, 49 C) for minimal medium, dansyl-chloride derivatization + Zorbax Eclipse C18 (methanol gradient, 286 nm, 30 C) for LB medium; glycerol time-course by HPLC-RID (MetaCarb 87H, 6.57 mM H2SO4); GlpK kinetics via PK/LDH-coupled NADH decay at A340 (0-10 mM FBP for allostery); intracellular cAMP by commercial ELISA; RNA-seq (HiSeq 50-cycle SE); RT-qPCR of glpK (rrsA/ihfB normalization); WGS resequencing (MiSeq).

EPOCH2 plate reader/spectrophotometer (BioTek); Cedex Bio Analyzer (Roche); Nexera LC-40 HPLC with RID-20A RI detector and UV detectors (Shimadzu); MiSeq and HiSeq sequencers (Illumina); StepOnePlus Real-Time PCR System (Applied Biosystems); MicroPulser electroporator (Bio-Rad); Qubit 2.0 fluorometer; TapeStation 2200; Econo-Pac Ni-NTA chromatography setup.

DESeq2 for DEG calling (fold change > 2 and adjusted P < 0.01); CLC Genomics Workbench read trimming (quality limit 0.05) and mapping to NC_017635.1 (mismatch cost 2, indel cost 3, length/similarity 0.9); independent t-tests (growth/GUR fold-changes with p-values); one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc (cAMP, acetate); SigmaPlot 12 curve fitting of allosteric inhibition Eq. (4) (K0.5, Hill coefficient); generation number Eq. (1); rate equations Eqs. (2)-(3); CRP-regulon enrichment vs RegulonDB annotation; growth rate used as proxy for growth-coupled GABA optimization.

CY02 specific growth rate in M9-glycerol improved ~40% (0.67 +/- 0.03 to 0.94 +/- 0.01 /hr) with significantly increased glycerol uptake; glpK^m explained most fitness gain (1.45-fold growth, 1.78-fold GUR; double 1.56-fold/1.70-fold; CY02 1.63-fold/1.60-fold), crp^m alone not significant; GlpK T235M lost FBP sensitivity (FBP K0.5 > 10,000 uM vs 386 uM WT; Vmax/Kcat essentially unchanged); glpK^m-harboring strains showed ~98% cAMP reduction, CY02 ~20% of WT, crp^m ~36%; 640 DEGs (149 up, 491 down) with CRP regulons over-represented > 2-fold; evolved strain showed acetate overflow (WT below detection); minimal-medium GABA identical (0.06 g/L both); LB + 2% glycerol: CY02 max titer 0.39 +/- 0.03 g/L and productivity 0.08 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr (~2.6-fold vs WT 0.15 g/L, 0.03 g/L/hr); single KOs lowered titer, doubles higher (0.45-0.46 g/L), CY02_TKO best 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L and 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr (3.9- and 4.3-fold vs WT); knockout benefit absent in wild-type background (epistasis with evolved genotype).

objective.value: Construct an Escherichia coli W derivative with improved gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) production from glycerol by combining adaptive laboratory evolution (1300 generations under glycerol limitation) with rational metabolic engineering (deletion of ackA, mgsA, gabT), and decipher the molecular basis of glycerol adaptation (mutation profiling, enzyme kinetics, transcriptomics).

hypothesis.value: ALE-improved glycerol uptake/utilization translates into superior growth-coupled GABA production, and redirecting acetate-overflow flux while blocking the methylglyoxal bypass and the GABA shunt in the evolved background further increases GABA titer and productivity.
